authority.scope: Relative codes 6/8/A/C represent soft pointers, codes 6/8 have zero-length payloads; BLOCK_HEADER has soft first/last entity and INSERT references.

bug: The parser accepted relative soft-pointer codes on first/last entity and INSERT fields but read their encoded offset as an absolute handle. It also narrowed wider common and body references into the 32-bit model.
change: Resolve accepted soft-pointer references against the containing BLOCK_HEADER handle using the existing bounded reader; reject out-of-range common and body handles and nonzero payloads on relative +1/-1 codes. Parsing failure resets the record and invalidates the input.

validation.baseline: Independently authored AC1012, AC1014, AC1015 and AC1018 bodies reproduced incorrect first/last or INSERT targets and silent wide-handle acceptance before the fix.
validation.focused: The new fast test checks relative 6/8/A/C on each applicable first/last and INSERT field, relative block-control compatibility, wide control, reactor, extension-dictionary and applicable body handles, malformed relative lengths, arithmetic underflow and overflow, reset and corrected retry.
validation.asan: Fully instrumented library and focused test pass under AddressSanitizer.

limits: The relative-source controls are hand-authored codec vectors, not a native producer witness.
The fix does not bind the captured BLOCK_HEADER body to the output graph or resolve dictionary merge semantics. Legacy LAYOUT output remains refused.
Existing historical model/paper-space ownership tolerance is unchanged.
